about: The iPhone app's performance budgets, held by PerfTests.swift on a simulator against a dev node with a busy fleet (scripts/dev-node.ts --heavy --auto-approve). A number over its limit fails the test. Where the X2 study's target (26 November 2026) is not met yet, the limit holds what was measured from getting worse, and the target is checked too, its miss recorded in every run as an expected failure until it is met. Launch is held from the app's own first line to Home's first frame with what it shows: before that is the platform's (on a simulator the process and its loader, and the libraries XCUITest and a device panel's tooling put into the app: 1.5–3.5 s measured), which the suite reports but can't hold the app to. Measured 26 November 2026, iOS 27.0 simulator, Debug (I9): the app's own launch 0.83–1.0 s under XCUITest (0.42–0.45 s launched plainly), CPU at rest 0.0–3.7 % over three runs, 8.8 ms a second of late frames scrolling. Measured again the same day on CI's Mac, the mini's iOS 27.2 simulator, Debug (I10), the app's first line now before it reads its key and its kept agents: its own launch 0.52 s under XCUITest when the Mac was quiet and up to 1.01 s when it wasn't (0.27–0.54 s launched plainly), something needing you on screen in 0.16–0.21 s at the 95th percentile, a dead link back in 0.94–1.02 s, 40–43 MB and 0.1 % of a core at rest. So three limits were tightened, each with room for a busy CI Mac: the event to 0.5 s, back to 1.5 s, memory to 80 MB. Launch keeps 1.5 s (a busy Mac doubles it), CPU at rest 5 % (I9 saw 3.7 % once), requests at rest X2's 2, a dead link noticed 5 s (three of the node's beats are 4.5 s), and scrolling 15 ms a second on the best of its three rounds (as measured since 26 November; since 28 November your agent's chat, where the app opens and Work is no more, measured as Home's list and Work's were). A minute with a stall in it (PerfTests.testRequestsThroughAStall, 26 November 2026: the node silent until the app takes its stream for dead after three of its beats and opens another) is held to rest's 2: the stream resumes from where it left off, so the stall costs the one request that opens it again (before, the new stream read every route again: 13 requests in the minute with the dev node stopped for 6 s on CI's Mac, the kind of stall its load near 480 made when testRequestsAtRest failed there), and the second is room for the stream being renewed twice. The first event after opening is held on its own to 1 s (eventToScreenFirstMs, 27 November 2026): it takes the path cold, and on CI's loaded Mac (PR #72) one such took 554 ms against 130–140 for the nine after it, which failed the steady limit, as the 95th percentile of ten is their largest; measured alone on the mini at loads of 64–115 on its 18 cores, main and that stack alike, a first took 138–173 ms and the rest 129–172. So it keeps its own limit, a first event that got slower still failing, and the ten after it keep 0.5 s. Change a limit only on purpose, in its own reviewed change, saying why.
